column2: Competition Commission of India v. State of Mizoram & Ors.
column3: Civil Appeal Nos. 10820-10822 of 2014 (with C.A. 1797 of 2015)
column12: Whether CCI can look into bid rigging in lottery tenders when lotteries are res extra commercium.
column13: Yes. The lottery trade being regulated does not take collusive bidding outside the Act; the High Court order was set aside and the CCI inquiry continues.
column14: CCI v. Bharti Airtel Ltd. (2019) 2 SCC 521

column2: Coal India Ltd. & Anr. v. Competition Commission of India & Anr.
column12: Whether the Competition Act applies to Coal India despite the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act and Art 39(b).
column13: It does. A government company with a statutory monopoly is an enterprise under the Act; the appeal was sent to be heard on its own merits.
column14: Ashoka Smokeless Coal India (P) Ltd. v. Union of India (2007) 2 SCC 640

column2: Independent Sugar Corporation Ltd. v. Girish Sriram Juneja & Ors.
column11: proviso to s 31(4) IBC; s 29 Competition Act
column12: Whether CCI approval of a combination must come before the CoC approves an insolvency resolution plan.
column13: Prior CCI approval is mandatory. The AGI Greenpac plan was set aside and the CoC was told to reconsider the plans.
column14: Committee of Creditors of Essar Steel India Ltd. v. Satish Kumar Gupta (2020) 8 SCC 531

column2: Competition Commission of India v. Schott Glass India Pvt. Ltd. & Anr.
column3: 2025 INSC 668 (Civil Appeal No. 5843 of 2014 with C.A. 9998 of 2014)
column12: Whether Schott's volume rebates, long-term supply deal and alleged tying were an abuse of dominance.
column13: No abuse shown. Conduct must be judged by its actual effect on competition, and the DG probe was flawed because cross-examination was refused.
column14: Excel Crop Care Ltd. v. CCI (2017) 8 SCC 47

column2: Competition Commission of India v. Independent Sugar Corporation Ltd. & Anr. (review)
column3: R.P.(C) No. 482 of 2025 in Civil Appeal No. 4924 of 2023
column12: Whether s 29 forces the CCI to send every combination to the DG after a show cause notice.
column13: No. The notice under s 29(1) is mandatory, but a DG reference under s 29(1A) is the CCI's choice; paras 128-131 of the January judgment were replaced.
column14: P.T. Rajan v. T.P.M. Sahir (2003) 8 SCC 498

column2: Competition Commission of India v. Monsanto Holdings Pvt. Ltd. & Ors.
column3: SLP(C) No. 25026 of 2023 and connected SLPs
column12: Whether the CCI probe into patent licensing terms could go on after the informants settled with the patentees.
column13: Court refused to interfere with the Delhi HC order quashing the probe, as the settlement removed its basis; the Patents Act v. Competition Act question was kept open.
column14: None cited; rests on Delhi HC judgment in Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson v. CCI (13-07-2023)

column2: Competition Commission of India v. Kerala Film Exhibitors Federation & Ors.
column11: s 3(3)(b) r/w s 27 and s 48 Competition Act
column12: Whether office-bearers of a trade body needed a second show cause notice before penalty, and whether the penalty was excessive.
column13: One notice was enough and the penalty was proportionate. The CCI order, including the two-year bar on the office-bearers, was restored.
column14: CCI v. Steel Authority of India Ltd. (2010) 10 SCC 744

column2: Flipkart India Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. v. Competition Commission of India & Ors.
column12: Whether the NCLAT's direction for a DG probe into Flipkart could stand once the tax findings it relied on were set aside by the ITAT.
column13: NCLAT order set aside and the appeal sent back to the NCLAT to decide afresh whether a prima facie case exists, applying Coal India.

column2: Amazon.com NV Investment Holdings LLC v. Competition Commission of India & Ors.
column11: s 45(2) r/w s 20(1) and s 31(1) Competition Act
column12: Whether the CCI could keep its 2019 approval of the Amazon-Future Coupons deal in abeyance and impose penalties for non-disclosure.
column13: No. s 45(2) is a penal provision, not a review power; the action was also out of time under s 20(1). CCI and NCLAT orders set aside and penalties to be refunded.
column14: Mangalore Chemicals & Fertilisers Ltd. v. Dy. Commissioner of Commercial Taxes (1992)
